Q: Couldn't find a working/matching GHC installation. Consider installing ghc-9.10.1 via ghcup or build HLS from source A:

This error message is a bit of a blanket kind. Maybe your root cause is same as it happened to me. Open a shell in a terminal, change directory to your project, and try running haskell-language-server-wrapper command (run it with an absolute path from ~/.ghcup/bin/ if it's not in PATH in your shell).

In my case, I've got the output end with

2026-06-27T18:19:24.355545Z | Debug | /usr/bin/ghc --print-libdir
GHC ABIs don't match!

Expected: Cabal-3.14.1.0:5df70b01f8da7b05ec99b0ee1eeb2e7c Cabal-syntax-3.14.1.0:… array-0.5.8.0:… base-4.21.0.0:… binary-0.8.9.3:… bytestring-0.12.2.0:… containers-0.7:… deepseq-1.5.1.0:… directory-1.3.9.0:… exceptions-0.10.9:… file-io-0.1.5:… filepath-1.5.4.0:… ghc-9.12.2:82286cd7d626e21a982319b5ca9a7fb7 ghc-bignum-1.3:… ghc-boot-9.12.2:… ghc-boot-th-9.12.2:… ghc-compact-0.1.0.0:… ghc-experimental-9.1202.0:… ghc-heap-9.12.2:… ghc-internal-9.1202.0:… ghc-platform-0.1.0.0:fa2ee5242385f86b6c03ee9e2a22933c ghc-prim-0.13.0:… ghc-toolchain-0.1.0.0:… ghci-9.12.2:… haddock-api-2.30.0:… haddock-library-1.11.0:… haskeline-0.8.2.1:… …
Got:      Cabal-3.14.1.0:3f0e2e49c018560a08ecb79253388681 Cabal-syntax-3.14.1.0:… array-0.5.8.0:… base-4.21.0.0:… binary-0.8.9.3:… bytestring-0.12.2.0:… containers-0.7:… deepseq-1.5.1.0:… directory-1.3.9.0:… exceptions-0.10.9:… file-io-0.1.5:… filepath-1.5.4.0:… ghc-9.12.2:db596df28bc150fb98711c40bd38b7fb ghc-bignum-1.3:… ghc-boot-9.12.2:… ghc-boot-th-9.12.2:… ghc-compact-0.1.0.0:… ghc-experimental-9.1202.0:… ghc-heap-9.12.2:… ghc-internal-9.1202.0:… ghc-platform-0.1.0.0:de400815b17c8ec4e0110534b01c2016 ghc-prim-0.13.0:… ghc-toolchain-0.1.0.0:… ghci-9.12.2:… …
Content-Length: 203

{"jsonrpc":"2.0", "method":"window/showMessage", "params": {"type": 1, "message": "Couldn't find a working/matching GHC installation. Consider installing ghc-9.12.2 via ghcup or build HLS from source."}}

Note the GHC differs only in hash among these.

And I thus knew to try building HLS from source — this is possible in the "Advanced options" accessible by pressing the Enter key in ghcup tui. You need to

  • check the set parameter so that it becomes selected after it's compiled,
  • set the jobs to something like 8 — it took a bit over half an hour on my ultrabook.
  • And pick target GHC versions to suit you.

It worked in my case after that! (It didn't make a difference that for me it happened in Emacs with Eglot.)

Q: Run libreoffice calc macro when a value is added to a column A:

In LibreOffice Calc, the “Content changed” event is part of the Sheet Events list, which you can access via the sheet’s context menu.

  • Copilot Search (in Microsoft Edge) misleadingly says to use Tools | Customize | Events

  • But that won't detect changes in a cell - only events affecting the entire spreadsheet.

Q: How can I implement a physical-entropy-based TRNG architecture in C/C++ on Windows 10 without external libraries? A:

Did you try the standard C++ header <random>? You can get much more from this header or it's boost counterpart. This is a short sample that illustrates POSIX entropy source usage. On windows, random_device ignores constructor arguments, and always uses a none-deterministic entropy source.

Q: Use existing MSYS2 install for Git-Bash, or any other way to avoid having two concurrent MINGWs A:

MSYS2's Git package runs in its Cygwin-like POSIX emulation environment, meaning it can be slower than Git Bash and handle certain situations worse. I know someone who uses Git Bash because he sometimes does a git pull while files are in use by a process, and Git Bash will handle that situation gracefully while MSYS2's Git just aborts and leaves things in a messy state. I still like using MSYS2 Git though.

Run this in any MSYS2 environment to make sure it's installed:

pacman -S --needed git

Put code like this in your .bashrc to get the branch displayed in your prompt:

source /usr/share/git/git-prompt.sh
PS1='\[\033[0m\]\[\033[32m\]\u@\h \[\e[35m\]$MSYSTEM\[\e[0m\] \[\033[33m\]\w$(__git_ps1 " (%s)")'$'\[\033[0m\]\n$ '

Q: What is *.servicebus.windows.net used for in Azure Data Factory? A:

It's not data, but instructions. If you look at the webpage on creating self-hosted integration run times it states this:

Azure Data Factory communicates with the self-hosted integration runtime to schedule and manage jobs. Communication is via a control channel that uses a shared Azure Service Bus Relay connection

Basically Factory is saying to integration runtime "Do you want me to do anything?". You do not have to provision or configure Service Bus so I wouldn't worry about it too much.

Q: sphinx-apidoc usage - multiple source python directories A:

The key is to:

  1. take ownership of modules.rst.
  2. run sphinx-apidoc multiple while suppressing generation of modules.rst.

For step 1, I run sphinx-apidoc normally to generate the modules.rst, then add the extra entries (and any tweaks), then check it in:

Sources               <<< customised title
========

.. toctree::
   :maxdepth: 4

   api                <<< default/first entry added sphinx-apidoc
   bin                <<< extra entry
   diagnostics        <<< extra entry
   project            <<< extra entry

For step 2, use the --no-toc option:

    sphinx-apidoc --no-toc -M -q -o $STAGEDIR/modules $PY_SRC/api
    sphinx-apidoc --no-toc -M -q -o $STAGEDIR/modules $PY_SRC/bin
    sphinx-apidoc --no-toc -M -q -o $STAGEDIR/modules $PY_SRC/diagnostics
    sphinx-apidoc --no-toc -M -q -o $STAGEDIR/modules $PY_SRC/paiyroll $PY_SRC/diagnostics/omit1 other_omit etc
